newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Teletas sees 50 pct rise in 1996 sales.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Teletas sees 50 pct rise in 1996 sales.

text.p: Turkish telecommunications equipment producer Alcatel Teletas Telekomunikasyon Endustri Ticaret A.S. expects to increase its total sales to $125 million this year from $80 million in 1995, a senior company offical said.

"A big portion of the total sales, almost $100 million, comes from our domestic sales to (state-owned) Turk Telekom, and the rest from our exports to Central Asian republics," general manager Lutfi Yenel told Reuters in an interview.
Alcatel Teletas is owned 39-percent by Alcatel Bell and 26 percent by Alcatel Holding BV within the French Alcatel Alsthom Group.
Yenel said new tenders opened by Turk Telekom helped Teletas increase its capacity utilisation ratio (CUR) to around 60 percent from 50 percent in 1995.

"We increased our stake in the domestic telecommunications market (Turk Telekom). Our stake in small and large communication systems has climbed up to 50 percent and protected our leading position in transmission systems."
Turk Telekom is the major buyer of telecommunications system in the domestic market. Turkey is planning to privatise part of Turk Telekom next year.
Teletas shares were traded 5,200-5,300 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange this morning. The shares fluctuated in a band of 3,200 lira and 7,400 lira throughout the year.
Analaysts say the company's dependence on only a single buyer -- Turk Telekom -- might hinder its prospects for growth.
Yenel, however, said Teletas was taking various measures.

"Our primary target is to increase exports to the Central Asian countries, like Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tadjikstan, and the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. We have done well so far particularly in the Georgian an Azerbaijan markets."
In July, Teletas won a $9.5 million tender to install digital switches and accompanying transmission systems in Georgia.
"Our second target is to sell unique products, like payphones, to all around the world," Yenel said.
He said Teletas sought to be become more active in the domestic market and increase the number of its customers as new operators enter into the telecomunications sector.
"With all these efforts, we will not be dependent on only one market. We will be a company with various customers within three or four years," he said.
Teletas doubled its net profit to 401.79 billion lira in the first half of 1996, against 199.03 billion in the same period of 1995.
Its net sales soared to 4.5 trillion lira from 1.7 trillion.

Teletas has recently sold one of its plants, which concentrated on part production, in Istanbul for $11 million. Yenel said the deal was part of Teletas' drive to focus on its core business and leave the part production busienss.
